Site.name: Under the Hood
Site.tagline: Senior and FAANG interview prep through mechanisms, not memorization
Site.description: Interactive, animated lessons on algorithms, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js and system design — explained at the level of how things actually work.

Home.title: Understand how it works — then you can explain it in any interview.
Home.lead: Algorithms, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js and system design — each topic explained in plain words first, then shown step by step in an animation you can play, pause and rewind.
Home.stats: {lessons} lessons · {viz} interactive visualizers · Uzbek and English
Home.how1Body: Each lesson opens with an everyday analogy, so you know what the idea is before any jargon.
Home.how2Body: Play the algorithm step by step on your own input. The current line of code and the reason for each step stay in view.
Home.how3Body: Real code, trade-offs, interview questions and a short quiz — then the lesson goes into your spaced-repetition list.

start.title: Getting started
start.description: How the platform works and how to study with it.

dsa.title: Algorithms & Data Structures
dsa.description: Patterns, not problem lists: recognition signals, templates, complexity and classic problems.

javascript.title: JavaScript
javascript.description: Event loop, execution contexts, closures, prototypes, GC and V8 — at the mechanism level.

typescript.title: Advanced TypeScript
typescript.description: Structural typing, generics and variance, conditional and mapped types, type-level puzzles.

react.title: React
react.description: Render vs commit, reconciliation, Fiber, hooks internals, concurrency and Server Components.

nextjs.title: Next.js
nextjs.description: App Router architecture, rendering strategies, RSC payload, hydration and caching.

nodejs.title: Node.js
nodejs.description: Event loop phases, libuv and the thread pool, streams and backpressure, production hygiene.

system-design.title: System Design
system-design.description: Backend and frontend system design with diagrams, plus an interview framework.

interview.title: Interview preparation
interview.description: The coding interview process, behavioral (STAR) and senior-level signals.

Progress.reviewLead: Spaced repetition: each successful review pushes the next one further out (1 → 3 → 7 → 16 → 35 days). Try to recall the TL;DR and the mechanism before opening the lesson.
Progress.reviewEmpty: Your review list is empty. Add lessons with “Add to review”.

Resources.title: Go deeper
Resources.pageLead: Courses, books and official documentation for each section. Every link was checked to exist; the date shows when.
Resources.uzNote: No Uzbek-language resources have been verified yet.

Puzzle.title: Type puzzle
Puzzle.limit: Code is checked on the server with the TypeScript compiler; it is never executed.

Principles.title: Programming principles
Principles.lead: SOLID, DRY, KISS, YAGNI and the other principles behind code that is easy to change. Every principle comes with a step-by-step animation, a bad and a good TypeScript example, and when not to apply it.
Principles.solidLead: Five letters, one goal: classes that are small, replaceable and safe to extend.

Glossary.title: Glossary
Glossary.lead: Short, plain definitions of the technical terms used in the lessons — from Big-O and closures to Cache Components and CRDTs. Terms stay in English in both languages; only the explanation is translated.
